originalTitle: Quicksilver Amy Hunt flies to glorious golden double with 200m triumph
summary: Britain’s Amy Hunt struck gold in the 200m to complete the sprint double, while Mark English became Ireland’s first European Championship men’s gold medallist by winning the 800m
content: Amid the adrenalised delirium of her second European title in three days, Amy Hunt walked to the nearest TV camera, held up her hands and, in homage to Russell Crowe’s character in Gladiator screamed: “Are you not entertained?” It quickly transpired that the 24-year-old Cambridge graduate had been quite the warrior off the track too. Because, as she revealed after collecting a 200m gold medal to go alongside Monday’s 100m title, she has been nearly fainting this year when running over the longer distance. “I have had a lot of health things going on this year – some really, really low pressure,” Hunt explained. “The 200s have been really scary. I have been nearly fainting after a lot of my 200s this year. I had just to go into that one and get on the bend and be really brave.” Hunt had entered the 200m final as the overwhelming favourite, but she had to work to chase down the two-time champion, Dina Asher-Smith, one lane outside her, around the bend. Having done that, the raucous 20,000 crowd at the Alexander Stadium expected to see a coronation. Instead it turned into a struggle, and Hunt only just had enough in the tank to cross the line in 22.19sec, ahead of Ireland’s fast-finishing Rhasidat Adeleke, who ran a national record of 22.28. Britain’s Asher-Smith took bronze a further 0.01 further back. It means that Hunt’s dream of winning an historic quadruple of gold medals at these European Championships is alive – as she made clear afterwards by holding two fingers up in her right hand, before flipping the hand to show four fingers. “Two out of four,” she said. “Honestly, I think the 100 is the hardest mentally. And the 200 is the hardest physically. “I was thinking about my coach,” he said before I went in: ‘Just imagine me in lane 10 with a stopwatch and a whistle. Just keep those thighs up, girl.’ “But there’s no celebrating, no champagne until Sunday night because I have a debt to the ladies,” Hunt explained, as she set her sights on the 4x100m and mixed relays over the weekend. “We have to make sure we come here and make sure we show them who is the best sprint nation in Europe. After 92 years, Ireland finally has a male European championship gold medallist. And his name is English – Mark English. The 33-year-old doctor from Donegal, produced a surgical performance to take gold, tracking and then overtaking Croatian Marino Bloudek in the home straight to win in 1:45.26. “Just relief,” said English. “I have been trying for a lifetime to get a title. I had planned to go to Sierra Nevada at 6am tomorrow, so I’m going to have to try to rebook that flight. These moments don’t come around often. I have a life that’s never come around for me before, so I’ll have to try to celebrate it somehow.” Bloudek clung on to take silver with Spain’s Mohamed Attaoui winning bronze. As the huge Irish contingent celebrated, the heart also went out to Britain’s Max Burgin, who was forced to pull out minutes before the race after suffering an injury in the warmup. It caps a summer of woe for Burgin, who also picked up a virus at the Commonwealth Games and didn’t make it out of the semi-finals. There was also no medal for another British contender, Elise Thorner, in the 3,000m steeplechase. The 25-year-old had entered the race as the fastest European over the distance in 2026 but she could only finish fifth behind Germany’s Gesa Felicitas Krause. The race was also notable for a faceplant by another German, Lea Meyer, into the water jump while running in the medal positions. While Meyer got up, she could only finish fourth. “It was gutting to see Lea actually fall, because I know her quite well,” said Thorner. “She is an amazing athlete. Shocking to see and trying to get over was a bit mad. But I was pretty spent with 200m so I was hanging on anyway.” Further success Germany as Leo Neugebauer hung on to win the men’s decathlon from his compatriot Niklas Kaul after collapsing over the line. His score of 8,611 points proved enough by 38 points, even though the 6ft 7in Neugebauer looked to be wading through treacle over the last 50 metres before collapsing over the line. But the event was marred by extraordinary scenes earlier on day two in the pole vault, after officials forgot to raise the bar from 4.70m to 4.80m. As a result athletes were under the impression that they were attempting 4.80m, while the bar was in fact still at 4.70m. A European Athletics statement said that the “results of this additional 4.70m round were cancelled, and the competition was resumed at 4.80m, with all athletes given the opportunity to attempt the height.”
chineseTitle: 快银艾米·亨特 (Amy Hunt) 夺得 200 米金牌
chineseSummary: 英国选手艾米·亨特 (Amy Hunt) 在 200 米比赛中夺得金牌，完成了短跑双打，而马克·英格利希 (Mark English) 在 800 米比赛中夺得金牌，成为爱尔兰第一位欧洲锦标赛男子金牌获得者
chineseContent: 艾米·亨特在三天内第二次获得欧洲冠军的兴奋中，走到最近的电视摄像机前，举起双手，向罗素·克劳在《角斗士》中扮演的角色致敬，尖叫道：“你不高兴吗？”很快我们就发现，这位 24 岁的剑桥毕业生在赛场外也是一位勇士。因为，正如她在周一获得 100m 冠军并获得 200m 金牌后透露的那样，今年她在跑较长距离时几乎晕倒。 “今年我的健康发生了很多事情——有些压力非常非常低，”亨特解释道。 “200 英里真的很可怕。今年，在我跑了很多次 200 英里之后，我几乎要晕倒了。我必须要勇敢地进入那个弯道。”亨特以压倒性优势进入 200 米决赛，但她必须努力追赶两届冠军迪娜·阿舍-史密斯（Dina Asher-Smith），她就在她外一条车道的拐弯处。完成这一切后，亚历山大体育场喧闹的 20,000 名观众期待着看到加冕典礼。相反，比赛变成了一场斗争，亨特的油箱里的油量刚刚够，他以 22.19 秒的成绩冲过终点线，领先于爱尔兰的快速完赛的拉西达特·阿德莱克 (Rhasidat Adeleke)，后者创下了 22.28 秒的全国纪录。英国选手阿舍-史密斯又落后0.01分获得铜牌。这意味着亨特在欧洲锦标赛上历史性地赢得四枚金牌的梦想已经实现——正如她随后用右手举起两根手指，然后翻转右手以露出四根手指所表明的那样。 “四分之二，”她说。 “老实说，我认为 100 米是心理上最难的。而 200 米是身体上最难的。“我在想我的教练，”我进去之前他说：“想象一下我在 10 号泳道，带着秒表和哨子。J
